role.altitude: The anesthesiologist keeps assessing patients, deciding anesthesia and treatment, teaching at the bedside and running drills; typing notes, transcribing questionnaires and writing teaching handouts shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Validating drafted notes quickly and keeping order sets current
role.ambitious_version: An anesthesiologist whose pre-op clinic notes are done when the patient leaves the room.

tasks.short: Explain anesthesia methods and complications to students and staff in the OR, run emergency drills, prepare teaching summaries, answer protocol questions and record training.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist informs students and staff in the OR of types and methods of anesthesia administration and signs of complications
Anesthesiologist runs emergency drills on methods to counteract reactions
Staff sign in to the drill in the learning system
Anesthesiologist prepares teaching summaries and drill scenarios

loop.input: The department's approved protocols on the chosen topic.
loop.output: A draft one-page teaching summary or drill scenario with signs, steps and doses.
loop.check: Every step and dose must quote the protocol section it comes from, or it is marked. A second check reads each step against its quoted section and marks steps the section does not support; the anesthesiologist reads the whole draft, checks every dose against the protocol and rewrites marked parts before use.
loop.stop: One draft per topic and protocol version.
loop.why_not_simpler: Protocols are written for reference; teaching needs a short sequence.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist answers staff questions on protocols outside cases
Anesthesiologist records who attended training and drills: in a spreadsheet today; after the change checks the sign-in list and adds those who did not sign in

tasks.design: Teaching in the OR and drills stay hands-on. A bounded step drafts one-page teaching summaries and drill scenarios from the department's approved protocols, citing each section, and the anesthesiologist checks every dose. Protocols are searchable on the department's intranet page, so staff look up more themselves. Staff sign in to a drill in the hospital's {LMS}, and the anesthesiologist checks the list and adds those who did not sign in.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts were written from scratch and protocol questions came to whoever was on duty.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that summarise approved documents with citations, and LMS sign-in.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a nurse the first sign of a reaction on a real patient.
tasks.altitude: Less writing of handouts; teaching stays at the bedside.

reach.learn: Whether short summaries are used during drills.

evidence.claim: Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: know the risks, train staff, test and monitor.
Language models can summarise a fixed document with section citations.

assumptions: Boundary: teaching staff and students about anesthesia; patient care is separate.
Input contract for s3: the department's approved protocols in the document system; drafts never use patient records.
Input contract for s4: protocols indexed on the intranet by the department secretary; questions about a live patient still go to the anesthesiologist.

OR teaching and drills keep their full time. s3 keeps 70 because the anesthesiologist reads, checks and edits each draft; s4 keeps 85 because only simple look-ups move to staff; s5 keeps 30 for checking the sign-in list and adding missing names. Staff signing in (s2s) is outside the anesthesiologist's savings.
unknowns: How often teaching materials are revised.
research_questions: Do drill scenarios made from protocols match what staff meet in practice?

already_counted.description: Anesthesiologist checks every dose in drafted summaries against the protocol.

incremental.description: Anesthesiologist flags outdated protocols to the department.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts need heavy rewriting (s3 keeps 90) and few staff sign in (s5 keeps 70) (4.4); high: drafts need light edits and staff sign in (10.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the patient fill in the pre-operative questionnaire, review it with the record and test results, examine the patient, order and read tests, diagnose illnesses and anesthesia risk, and write the assessment note.

steps.what: Patient fills in the pre-operative health questionnaire in the patient portal
Anesthesiologist reviews the questionnaire, the record and earlier test reports
Anesthesiologist examines the patient: airway, heart and lungs
Anesthesiologist decides on and orders extra tests such as ECG or lab and reads the results
Anesthesiologist diagnoses illnesses relevant to anesthesia and sets the risk class
Anesthesiologist writes the pre-operative assessment note

loop.input: The consultation audio, recorded with the patient's consent, and the pre-operative note template.
loop.output: A draft assessment note in the template's headings.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript and every finding in the transcript missing from the draft; the anesthesiologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and edits the note before saving it. A monthly sample is compared with the audio for omissions.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template gives headings; the history comes as conversation.

tasks.design: Patients fill in the pre-operative questionnaire in the patient portal at home, so their answers arrive as fields in the hospital record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with risk answers highlighted. With the patient's consent, a certified scribe drafts the assessment note from the consultation and the anesthesiologist validates it. Examining, ordering tests and setting the risk class stay with the anesthesiologist; no software scores the patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper questionnaires were read and retyped, and notes typed during the consult.
tasks.enabler_now: Portal questionnaires that write to the record, and validated scribe notes.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who cannot fill in a questionnaire or forget important history.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a difficult airway at a glance.
tasks.altitude: A little less reading and typing; assessment stays with the anesthesiologist.

reach.learn: Whether portal questionnaires shorten the nurse's intake.

evidence.claim: A Dutch scribe drafts the note and the clinician validates it before it enters the hospital record.
In a Swedish health system, clinicians using a scribe self-estimated note time down 29% (three of seven authors from the vendor).
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: the pre-operative assessment; the anesthesia plan is part of it, the operation is outside.

Input contract for s2: answers entered by patients in the portal questionnaire (s1) with about the effort of the paper form; about 75% of patients use the portal; the rest fill in paper that the nurse enters.
Input contract for s6: consultation audio recorded by the scribe with consent, in about 80% of consults.

Examination, tests and the risk decision keep their full time; patient time is outside the anesthesiologist's savings. s2 keeps 80 because the answers sit beside the record with risk answers highlighted, and reading them and earlier reports stays; s6 keeps 75 because about 80% of consults are recorded and each draft is read against the consult and edited.
unknowns: Share of patients who use the portal.
research_questions: Do missed risk factors change when patients fill in at home?

incremental.description: Anesthesiologist asks for and notes consent to record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the patients use the portal (s2 keeps 90) and half agree to recording (s6 keeps 85) (3.9); high: 75% portal use and 80% of consults recorded as assumed (7.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise residents in the OR, teach anesthesiology principles in lectures and case discussions, prepare teaching material and assess residents in the portfolio.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist teaches anesthesiology principles to residents case by case in the OR
Anesthesiologist prepares lectures, quiz questions and case material

loop.input: The department's protocols and the guideline chosen for the session.
loop.output: Draft quiz questions with answers, each citing the protocol or guideline section.
loop.check: Every answer must quote the cited section, or the question is dropped. A second check reads each answer against its section and drops questions the section does not support; the anesthesiologist reads every question and answer before use. No patient data are used.
loop.why_not_simpler: A question bank holds old questions; new guidelines need new ones.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist gives lectures and leads case discussions
Anesthesiologist assesses residents' performance after the case
Anesthesiologist records the assessment in the residents' portfolio

tasks.design: Teaching in the OR, lectures and assessing residents stay with the anesthesiologist. A bounded step drafts quiz questions from the department's protocols and the chosen guideline with section citations, Assessment forms can be filled on a phone right after the case; writing the assessment keeps its time. No software assesses residents.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quiz questions were written by hand and assessments filled in at the end of the week.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that draft questions with citations, and mobile portfolio forms.
tasks.still_hard: Judging when a resident is ready to work alone.
tasks.human_edge: Letting a resident struggle just long enough to learn.
tasks.altitude: Nothing much changes; preparation is slightly faster.

reach.learn: Whether assessments filled right after cases are more specific.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft questions from a fixed document and cite the section used.
Using AI to evaluate learners' outcomes is an AI Act high-risk area; the design does not.

assumptions: Boundary: teaching and assessing residents; the training program itself is outside.
Input contract for s3: approved department protocols and published guidelines chosen by the anesthesiologist.
OR teaching, lectures, assessing and recording assessments keep their full time. s2 keeps 85 because only quiz questions are drafted and checked; lectures and case material are written as today.
research_questions: Do residents use the quiz sets to prepare?

incremental.description: Anesthesiologist keeps the question set current with protocol changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most drafted questions fail the check and are written by hand (s2 keeps 95) (0.5); high: drafted questions hold up (2.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide medical care and consultation in the wards, ICU and pain clinic, decide treatment, prescribe medication and treatment, write consultation notes, refer patients for surgery and answer nurses' calls.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist provides medical care and consultation on wards, in the ICU and the pain clinic
Anesthesiologist decides the treatment
Anesthesiologist prescribes medication and treatment in the record
Anesthesiologist checks the final prescription: drug, dose, route, timing and patient against the treatment decision and the medication check alerts
Anesthesiologist signs the checked prescription, releasing it to the pharmacy and ward nurses
Anesthesiologist writes the consultation note

loop.input: The consultation audio, recorded with the patient's consent where the setting allows.
loop.output: A draft consultation note with findings, advice and plan.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consult transcript; the anesthesiologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed statement and edits the note before saving it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The advice comes out of a conversation at the bedside.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist writes the referral note for surgery or another specialist

loop.output: A draft referral note with question, findings and medication.
loop.check: Medication and findings must match the record, or the line is marked. A second check reads each sentence against the validated consultation note and marks statements the note does not support; the anesthesiologist edits every marked line.
loop.why_not_simpler: The referral restates the note for a different reader.

steps.what: Anesthesiologist checks the final referral: question, findings and medication against the record, and the specialist it goes to
Anesthesiologist sends the checked referral through the record
Anesthesiologist answers nurses' calls about patients

tasks.design: Care, consultation and treatment decisions stay with the anesthesiologist. Order sets for standard pain and post-operative regimens shorten prescribing, with the existing medication checks still running. Where the patient agrees and the setting allows, a scribe drafts the consultation note, and a referral note is drafted from the validated note; the anesthesiologist edits both, then checks the final referral and its addressee and sends it once through the record as today. Each prescription is checked and signed once before it reaches the pharmacy and nurses.

approvals.approved_version: The prescription with drug, dose, route and timing exactly as checked by the anesthesiologist in s3c, signed once for this patient and released to the pharmacy and ward; any change needs a new check and signature.
The referral note exactly as checked by the anesthesiologist in s5c, sent once through the record to the surgeon or specialist named there; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and referrals were typed after each consult, often late in the day.
tasks.enabler_now: Order sets in hospital records, scribes and referral letter drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Consults in the ICU where recording is not possible.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a patient's pain beyond the score.
tasks.altitude: A little less typing; care decisions do not change.

reach.learn: Whether order sets reduce calls to check doses.

evidence.claim: A Dutch tool drafts referral letters and suggests codes.
The Dutch drug database checks interactions, contraindications and doses.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software drafts, it does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: consultations and treatment outside the OR; anesthesia during surgery is separate.
Input contract for s3: order sets for standard regimens built by the department with the hospital pharmacist; about half of prescriptions fit an order set.
Input contract for s4: consultation audio recorded with consent in about 60% of consults; ICU and emergency consults are typed.

Care, decisions, nurse calls, and the checks and releases of prescriptions and referrals keep their full time. s3 keeps 80 because about half of prescriptions fit an order set; s4 keeps 75 because about 60% of consults are recorded and each draft is read and edited; s5 keeps 75 because the referral is drafted from the validated note and edited.
unknowns: Share of time spent in consultations outside the OR.
research_questions: Do notes get written sooner after consults?

already_counted.description: Anesthesiologist validates drafted notes and referrals.

incremental.description: Anesthesiologist reviews order sets with the pharmacist yearly.
Anesthesiologist asks for and notes the patient's consent to record the consult.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few prescriptions fit an order set (s3 keeps 95), only a third of consults are recorded (s4 keeps 87) and referral drafts need heavy edits (s5 keeps 90) (2.8); high: coverage as assumed (7.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
